references.text: The Lord spoke with Moses face to face, as a man speaks with his friend. This confirms the unique, direct communication between God and Moses.
No prophet arose in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face. This summarizes Moses' unique position among the prophets.
God showed Moses His glory but hid His face. Moses saw God's form in a way no one else did.
God spoke to Israel in night visions, showing how He often revealed Himself through visions, unlike the direct communication with Moses.
God reveals Himself to prophets through visions and dreams, but with Moses it was different - He spoke directly with him.
God speaks through riddles and parables through the prophet Ezekiel, unlike the clear, direct communication with Moses.
Proverbs mentions riddles and dark sayings, which stand in contrast to the clear revelation Moses received.
Moses was faithful in all God's house as a servant. This confirms Moses' unique position as God's servant.
No one has ever seen God, but the only Son has made Him known. Jesus surpasses Moses in His revelation of God.
We behold the Lord's glory with unveiled face. This connects to Moses' privilege of seeing God's form.
